header.title: Open Calculations Studio
header.heroAlt: Open Calculations Studio: check of an IPE 300 steel beam, with the text of the calculation on the left and the worked-out result with moments, shear forces and unity checks on the right
header.label: Structural calculations
header.tagline: Calculations your colleague can check in one read
header.desc: Write your calculation as text with units and see the worked-out result at once: formula, substituted values and outcome on one line. Start from a sheet for concrete, steel, timber, masonry or foundations, right in the browser.

meta.description: Free app for structural calculations in the browser: write your calculation as text with units and see the worked-out result straight away. With sheets for the Eurocodes and NEN 9997-1.
meta.title: Open Calculations Studio — OpenAEC Foundation

calc.alt: Punching shear calculation to EN 1992-1-1: on the left the text with units and conditions, on the right the worked-out formulas with substituted values
calc.title: Write the calculation the way you would on paper
calc.desc: Type a formula with units, such as d_eff = (d_y + d_z) / 2. The worked-out result appears at once as proper maths: formula, substituted values and outcome on one line, with the unit. Conditions pick the right formula, for example per column type.

codes.alt: Library of sheets per Eurocode, with EN 1995-1-1 Timber expanded and the full check of a timber beam opened
codes.title: Start from a code sheet instead of a blank page
codes.desc: Over fifty sheets per clause, from the load combinations in NEN-EN 1990 to bending, buckling and deflection in concrete, steel and timber, masonry and pile bearing capacity to NEN 9997-1. With full checks of a concrete beam, a steel beam and a timber beam.

input.alt: Wind load to NEN-EN 1991-1-4: drop-down lists for wind zone and terrain category and an input field for the reference height
input.title: Pick and fill in, the result follows
input.desc: A sheet can ask for input: a drop-down list for wind zone, strength class or consequence class, or a field for a height or span. Change a choice and the whole worked-out result recalculates at once.

review.alt: Only the worked-out result on screen: bending and shear of a concrete beam to EN 1992-1-1 with the unity check
review.title: Every step visible, no black box
review.desc: Hide the editor and read only the worked-out result, with the clause numbers of the code alongside. Whoever checks the calculation sees exactly which formula with which values leads to the unity check.

notice.text: The browser version calculates fully, but saving and exporting do not work there yet. The desktop app with projects and a structural report is not public yet.

units.title: Calculating with units
units.desc: mm, kN, N/mm², mm⁴ and all SI units. b*h becomes mm² by itself; 'to' converts to the unit you want.

chain.title: Formula, values and outcome
chain.desc: Every line shows name = formula = substituted values = result, with proper fractions, roots and Greek letters.

live.title: Live result
live.desc: Text on the left, result on the right. What you type is calculated straight away.

conditions.title: Conditions and loops
conditions.desc: #if, #else if and #else for 'passes' or 'fails', and #repeat and #for for series.

macros.title: Your own functions and tables
macros.desc: Macros with #def, matrices and lookup tables for material values.

calcpad.title: CalcPAD syntax
calcpad.desc: If you know CalcPAD, you will recognise the structure: headings, text lines, comments and commands work the same way.

en1990.title: Basis and combinations
en1990.desc: NEN-EN 1990: ultimate and serviceability limit states, EQU, accidental, seismic and design values.

loads.title: Loads
loads.desc: Imposed loads, snow and wind to EN 1991 with the Dutch annex, including a taller building nearby.

concrete.title: Concrete
concrete.desc: Bending, shear with and without stirrups, punching, crack width and deflection to EN 1992-1-1.

steel.title: Steel
steel.desc: Cross-section class, tension, compression, bending, shear, buckling, lateral-torsional buckling and bottom-flange bending to EN 1993-1-1.

timber.title: Timber
timber.desc: Bending, shear, compression, torsion, buckling, tapered beam, notch, deflection and floor and roof sheathing to EN 1995-1-1.

masonry.title: Masonry
masonry.desc: Compressive strength, wall in compression, shear and slenderness to EN 1996-1-1.

geo.title: Foundations
geo.desc: Strip footing, pile bearing capacity, settlement and sliding to NEN 9997-1.

examples.title: Worked examples
examples.desc: Examples from Vandepitte on shear stresses, deflection, buckling, natural frequency and virtual work.

select.title: Drop-down lists
select.desc: Choose consequence class, strength class, service class or pile type from a list; the calculation follows.

prompts.title: Input fields
prompts.desc: Values that differ per project, such as a height or a load, go into a field in the worked-out result.

gef.title: Read a cone test
gef.desc: A sheet can ask for a GEF file, so you can use the cone test data in your foundation calculation.

views.title: Three views
views.desc: Text and result side by side, the editor only or the result only.

editor.title: Colour-coded editor
editor.desc: Line numbers and colours for headings, commands and drop-down lists, so you keep track of long calculations.

free.title: No account
free.desc: Open the page and start. Your calculation runs in your own browser.

features.label: Features
features.heading: Calculate, check and have it reviewed
features.sub: Start with the highlights, or pick a topic.

timber.title: Torsion, tapered beam and notch
timber.desc: Three new timber sheets to EN 1995-1-1: §6.1.8, §6.4.2 and §6.5.2.

sheathing.title: Floor and roof sheathing
sheathing.desc: Check the boards or panels of a timber floor or roof.

flange.title: Bottom-flange bending
flange.desc: A steel beam with a wheel or hanging load on the bottom flange, as its own sheet.

wind.title: Wind near a taller building
wind.desc: The wind load uses Annex A.4 when there is a taller building nearby.

whatsnew.label: New in September 2026
whatsnew.title: More sheets for timber and steel
whatsnew.desc: The library in the browser gained new checks for timber and steel, and the wind calculation now takes a taller building nearby into account.

files.a: In the browser version you start from a sheet in the library or type your own. You can paste a calculation in CalcPAD syntax into the editor. A sheet can read a cone test as a GEF file. Opening files through the menu does not work in the browser yet.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: No. The browser version works straight away, without an account. There is also a desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux, with projects, calculation modules and a structural report, but its installers are not public yet.

price.q: What does Open Calculations Studio cost?
price.a: Nothing. The browser version is free, with no account or subscription.

save.q: In which format is my work saved?
save.a: Not yet in the browser version: saving and exporting to PDF, IFC, HTML or JSON do not work there yet. Copy your text to keep it. The desktop app saves a project as an .ifccalculation file.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: In any modern browser, on Windows, macOS and Linux. The calculating happens in your own browser.

practice.a: The sheets follow the Eurocodes with the Dutch national annexes and NEN 9997-1, with the clause numbers alongside. Always check the result yourself. In the desktop app, only the timber joist floor and the emergency roof overflow have been reviewed and released so far; the other modules are still marked for checking.

ifc.a: Not yet in the browser. The calculation engine can write a calculation as IFC4x3 and IFCX, so a check belongs to the right element in the BIM model; that is part of the desktop app.

source.a: Not yet. The repository on GitHub is not public yet; that is why this page has no downloads yet.

calcpad.q: How does it relate to CalcPAD?
calcpad.a: Open Calculations Studio is inspired by CalcPAD and supports a large part of its syntax: headings, text, conditions, loops, macros and plots. It runs in the browser, so on macOS and Linux too.

core.title: Own calculation engine
core.desc: Parser, evaluator and renderer in TypeScript, also usable as a library in other software.

mathjs.desc: Calculating with units and matrices, with automatic simplification of the unit.

katex.desc: Formulas as clean maths, with fractions, roots, subscripts and superscripts.

codemirror.desc: The editor with line numbers and colours for the calculation syntax.

ifc.title: IFC4x3 and IFCX
ifc.desc: The engine turns a calculation into IFC4x3 STEP and IFCX JSON-LD.

tauri.title: Vite and Tauri 2
tauri.desc: Vite builds the browser version; the desktop app uses a thin native shell in Rust.

tech.heading: Technology
tech.sub: For those who want to know how it is built.
